propositions: Six proposed deterministic clarity criteria each have historical counterexamples in closed, signed tickets that passed both plan-review and completion-verifier attestation.

Literal section-heading requirements reject valid tickets whose executable plans carry their mechanism in semantic aliases or non-heading compact formats (e.g., actionable What sections without an Approach heading).
Placeholder-free exact lexicon detectors flag bounded conditional work (e.g., 'check if') as deferred design when the condition is mechanically decidable and the action is fully specified.
Per-AC explicit proof markers are not necessary; precise behavioral oracles without verification-clause sentinels are sufficient and passed attestation in historical tickets.
Edit-set requirements are unsound for read-only analysis and operational work with explicit no-edit output contracts recorded in completion evidence.
Testing-section heading-triggered negative-scenario requirements are inapplicable to mechanical/non-user-facing work and should be gated on semantic applicability, not heading presence alone.
